sector_news_last_month: Nifty FMCG opened the month as the top-performing sectoral index on the NSE, aided by a sharp retreat in crude oil prices
Lower crude was seen easing pressure on packaging and petroleum-linked input costs, while also supporting India's broader inflation and household-consumption outlook
The sector had already outperformed the benchmark Nifty 50 over the preceding three months heading into July, a trend that continued into the new month
Q1 FY27 (April-June 2026) earnings season ran through the month, with most major FMCG companies scheduled to report results

Analyst previews pointed to a mixed quarter: home-and-personal-care companies were expected to see stronger revenue acceleration, while cigarette-linked profitability at ITC was expected to take a steep hit from a recent excise-duty increase

Brokerages flagged raw-material cost inflation as a broad headwind across the sector this quarter, with one proprietary FMCG input-cost index reported sharply higher year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter
Marico was repeatedly flagged as a rare exception, expected to benefit from softening prices in a key raw material even as most peers faced cost pressure
Food-and-beverage names such as Nestle India and Varun Beverages were expected to see a strong seasonal volume boost from favourable summer demand

Hindustan Unilever signalled plans for calibrated price hikes across categories from the following quarter, seen by analysts as a move to protect margins rather than boost profits, and viewed as a possible bellwether for similar action across the sector

Brokerages turned more constructive on FMCG valuations overall following the sector's earlier correction in the year, citing improving volume trends, expansion in quick-commerce channels and deeper rural distribution as supportive medium-term factors
A below-normal monsoon outlook was flagged as a risk to rural-linked demand across FMCG, alongside similarly rural-exposed sectors
GST-related tailwinds from the prior year's rate rationalisation continued to be cited as a supportive medium-term backdrop for volume growth across staples companies
